title: Give each acceptance field its own generator prompt sourcing that field's rule

facts.note: In scope: only the prompt/config files that generate acceptance fields. Out of scope: acceptance artifacts edited by hand.
Fires when someone authors or changes an acceptance-field generator prompt.
Tasks that explicitly concern composing or maintaining acceptance-field authoring prompts. A mention of harness, route, URN or acceptance on its own is not enough.

values: acceptance-field generator prompt added or modified (id, urn, harness, route, given, when, then)
facts.note: Needs a structural diff observer over the generator configuration to tell which field prompts changed.

values: generator prompts not split per field
a field prompt does not source its convention section or omits/weakens its field rule
facts.note: An LLM must judge whether a prompt's wording carries the field's rule.

fires: Planner writes the generator prompts/configuration that author acceptance fields (id, urn, harness, route, given, when, then).
Planner revises an existing acceptance-field generator prompt, e.g. the harness or route prompt.
Planner consolidates or splits acceptance-generation prompts.
doesNotFire: Planner creates or edits an acceptance by hand without using or changing any generator prompt. This rule does not require that acceptances be generated.
Coder implementing tests or production code for an acceptance that is already authored.
Editing prose or docs that only reference acceptance ids or fields and contain no acceptance-field generator prompt.

given: You are composing or maintaining the generator prompts that author acceptance fields
when: you write or change the prompt for any of id, urn, harness, route, given, when, then
then: Give each field its own prompt, and have that prompt source its field's section of the acceptance convention and state that section's rule as a requirement.
prefer: id prompt requires AC-{STEP}-{NNN}: step code + zero-padded index.
urn prompt requires derivation via URNBuilder.acceptance from wagon slug, WMBT ID, harness code, sequence.
harness prompt requires the harness that best exercises the outcome (unit/http/event/ws/e2e/...).
route prompt requires route.layers and route.sequence, flowing presentation -> application -> domain -> integration.
given prompt requires only needed preconditions (auth, builders, time, stubbing, knobs) before the action runs.
when prompt requires the trigger in the harness-specific shape (http request, unit target, event topic, etc.).
then prompt requires assertions proving the outcome (status, body, headers, error, metrics, etc.).
avoid: One generic prompt that writes all fields at once.

A field prompt that does not source its section, or that softens its rule (e.g. hand-built URNs, harness picked by habit, unneeded preconditions, generic triggers, assertions not tied to the outcome).
why: Each acceptance field has its own authoring rule in the acceptance convention, so each field's prompt sources that section.
evidence: The generator configuration has one prompt per field (id, urn, harness, route, given, when, then), and each prompt sources the matching section of the acceptance convention.
Each field prompt states its field rule (listed in prefer) as a requirement.
The generated acceptance id matches AC-{STEP}-{NNN}, with a zero-padded index.
The generated urn equals URNBuilder.acceptance(wagon slug, WMBT ID, harness code, sequence).
The generated route.layers and route.sequence are both populated and ordered presentation -> application -> domain -> integration.
The generated when uses the chosen harness's shape. The generated then contains assertions on the outcome (status, body, headers, error, metrics, ...).
verifier_detail: id pattern: AC-{STEP}-{NNN}. STEP is the step code and NNN is the zero-padded index.
Harness values include unit, http, event, ws and e2e. The list is open.
Route layer order: presentation -> application -> domain -> integration.
Term generator_prompt: the LLM authoring prompt for an acceptance field.
Scope: the rule governs the prompts. It does not require acceptances to be produced by generators, and acceptances edited by hand are out of scope.

splitSuggestion.then: Compose the acceptance id as AC-{STEP}-{NNN}, using the step code and a zero-padded index.
Derive the acceptance URN with URNBuilder.acceptance from wagon slug, WMBT ID, harness code and sequence.
Select the harness that best exercises the outcome.
Populate route.layers and route.sequence so actions flow presentation -> application -> domain -> integration.
Declare only the preconditions the action needs before it runs.
Describe the trigger in the shape of the chosen harness.
List assertions that prove the outcome.

additions.text: then now holds a single obligation: one prompt per field, which sources its convention section and states that section's rule as a requirement. The seven field-content rules (S012–S018) are independent obligations on acceptance artifacts. They are kept here as the mandatory content of each field prompt (prefer[0..6], restated in avoid[1]), and each should become its own convention (see splitSuggestion).
additions.justification: One-obligation rule, as the auditor required.

additions.text: prefer lists what each field prompt must require. This is the content the then obligation points to, not optional advice.
additions.justification: Keeps all seven source instructions mandatory and coder-facing without bundling them into then.

additions.text: The avoid items restate the per-prompt split and each field instruction as prompt anti-patterns.
additions.justification: Derived from S008 and S012–S018. No new obligation is added.

additions.text: Activation facts, fires and doesNotFire are authored, because the source has no activation section. They are scoped to composing or maintaining acceptance-field generator prompts, and acceptance edits made by hand are excluded.
additions.justification: The schema needs observable activation, and the auditor accepted this scope.

additions.text: The why only restates S006/S008: each field has its own rule, and each prompt sources its section. No further rationale is claimed.
additions.justification: The source gives no explicit rationale, so none is invented.

additions.text: Coder-facing text is about 1,250 characters because all seven field rules must remain in coder-facing fields.
